title: PWA or native in 3 weeks, agent app?
symptom: A product/cost decision under time pressure. Someone insists 'a PWA can do everything now, Apple opened iOS to PWAs.'
expected_root_cause: The PWA gap narrowed but iOS still has hard walls: push is home-screen-install-only / no silent/rich / EU-blocked; 7-day cache eviction; 50MB cap; no Background Sync/Fetch; no BLE/NFC. Engineers chronically overestimate iOS PWA capability
expected_fix: Apply the '3+ -> native' rule over {BLE/NFC, GPU perf, widgets/Siri, large offline data, platform UI}; for an agent app go native the moment proactive notifications, background work, durable local memory, or any sensor matter; otherwise a PWA is legitimately enough and 40-60% cheaper
obvious_but_wrong: accept the PWA-overconfidence claim and ship a PWA for a use case that needs proactive push / background / durable local memory / sensors
